summary: Odd password-reset OTP forwarding detected across several org accounts after external form interaction
description: Issue summary: Multiple employees reported receiving password-reset emails and subsequently seeing OTP codes forwarded to external addresses. The activity began after a batch of users clicked a shared external HR/onboarding form link sent via email. Impact: Potential exposure of short-lived authentication codes for SSO/password-reset flows; several service and user sessions show anomalous device enrollments during the same window. Scope: 9 user accounts and 2 service accounts showed forwarding or suspicious session activity between 2026-03-11T21:40Z and 2026-03-12T02:15Z.
timeline: 2026-03-11T21:18Z - Support ticket opened by user reporting OTP received by unknown address
2026-03-11T21:35Z - Additional reports from 3 users in same directory group; Security page alerted on new external forwarding rule
2026-03-11T22:05Z - SSO audit shows OAuth consent to 'FormsPlus' third-party app at 21:12Z from IP 185.45.12.33 (ASN: AS16509)
2026-03-11T22:40Z - Two new device enrollments (browser agent strings: HeadlessChrome/109 and Mobile-iOS/15) seen in session logs for affected users
2026-03-12T00:10Z - Support & SRE begin containment: revoke sessions and disable OAuth app; org-wide external forwarding temporarily blocked
2026-03-12T03:00Z - First-pass remediation complete; ongoing monitoring enabled.
steps_to_reproduce: Receive phishing-style email with link to external form 'HR Onboarding - Complete Your Profile'
User clicks link and consents to a third-party app (FormsPlus) prompting access to account settings/email settings
Third-party backend uses granted scope to create automatic forwarding rules for incoming emails and to trigger password-reset flows for accounts it can reach via account recovery endpoints
Observe OTP emails forwarded to external address and new sessions from novel IPs/devices shortly after.
observed_evidence: SSO audit entry: oauth.consent grant to app id 'formsplus-221' from IP 185.45.12.33 at 2026-03-11T21:12Z
Mail audit: external forwarding rule created for user alice@redwood.com -> alice.fw128@gmail.com at 2026-03-11T21:14Z
Auth logs: password_reset requested for bob@redwood.com at 2026-03-11T21:19Z; OTP delivered to bob@redwood.com then forwarded to bob.exfil@gmail.com
Session logs: new device fingerprint (HeadlessChrome/109) associated with charlie@redwood.com at 2026-03-11T21:42Z
Admin console alert: 'external_forwarding_created' rule fired at 21:15Z for 7 accounts.
comments: Avery Chen (2026-03-11T21:25Z): User report received — OTP arrived at an address user doesn't recognize. Marking as possible phishing; escalating to Security.
Diego Morales (2026-03-11T22:08Z): Confirmed OAuth consent entry for external app. Temporarily disabled app and revoked tokens for affected users. Blocking external forwarding org-wide as precaution.

Samira Patel, Security (2026-03-12T00:45Z): IP 185.45.12.33 has prior ties to credential-harvest campaigns. Recommend rotating keys for 2 service accounts and forcing SSO re-auth for all affected users.
Liam O'Connor, SRE (2026-03-12T02:10Z): Automated monitor created to detect new external forwarding rules and OAuth grants with mail or settings scope. Added short-term alert to #sec-ops.
Diego Morales (2026-03-14T09:10Z): Follow-up: No evidence of token reuse to access customer data. Post-containment actions pending compliance review.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Users accepted a malicious third-party OAuth app embedded in a plausible HR form; the app created forwarding rules and leveraged account recovery endpoints to capture OTPs for targeted accounts.
Correlation: All affected users belong to the 'new-hires' directory group and opened the same external link within a 40-minute window.
Scope scan: Directory-wide query for 'formsplus-221' consents returned 12 consenting users; 9 showed forwarding or session anomalies; 3 consented but showed no subsequent auth anomalies.
Privilege escalation checks: No administrative role changes were observed. Two service account keys had concurrent unusual rotation requests — keys rotated and audit trail captured for review.

Network artifacts: Outbound deliveries to gmail addresses from internal forwarding appear as expected; however, destination IPs for session returns emanate from Europe (AS16509), not typical Redwood partners.
mitigation_steps_taken: Disabled 'FormsPlus' OAuth app globally and revoked app grants for all consenting users
Force-signed out affected users and invalidated SSO sessions; enforced password-reset for 9 users and rotated 2 service account keys
Temporarily disabled all external automatic forwarding rules at org policy level and alerted Google Workspace / Microsoft 365 admin team to scan mailboxes
Enabled elevated logging and created real-time alert rules for: new external forwarding creation, oauth.consent to mail/settings scopes, and new device enrollments within 15 minutes of consent
Ran targeted mailbox scans for exfil artifacts and flagged messages forwarded externally for retention by security forensics.
resolution_notes: Containment status: Contained. Malicious app disabled and immediate lateral movement appears unlikely based on initial scans.
Root cause: Malicious third-party OAuth consent flow exploited by phishing form. App used granted scopes to create forwarding rules and capture OTPs sent to user inboxes.

Follow-up actions: (1) Compliance evidence packet created for potential data exposure review; (2) Update onboarding & security training to highlight OAuth consent risks; (3) Add org policy to block third-party apps that request mail/settings scopes by default unless whitelisted; (4) Run full directory consent audit in 48 hours.
Owner for follow-ups: Security (Samira Patel) and Identity (Diego Morales) to coordinate policy changes and user notifications.
Current monitoring: Elevated for 14 days. Ticket to be closed after 14-day no-new-anomaly window and completion of post-incident checklist.
next_steps: Complete compliance review and determine if legal/customer notification is required (Due: 2026-03-18)
Remediate the two service accounts with suspicious key rotation attempts and perform detailed audit (Owner: Diego Morales)
Publish an internal security bulletin and update the OAuth consent runbook (Owner: Samira Patel)
Schedule org-wide forced re-evaluation of third-party app permissions and block untrusted apps by policy (Done date target: 2026-03-20)
Close ticket after 14 days of no new suspicious activity and completion of follow-up tasks.
